newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures ended broadly firmer but most positions were below their ceiling on scale-up producer selling. January closed $22 higher at $1,340 per tonne while March added $21 to close at $1,310 per tonne.

In New York arabica futures closed sharply higher and the chart picture is displaying an increasingly bullish tone. The March/May switch, a barometer of nearby availability widened to 3.35 cents/lb, up from 2.05 cents on Monday.
The recent decline of US certified coffee stocks underlines current tight supplies. This points to firmer prices and traders said that $1.25 seems a probable target.

UNITED STATES - The coffee, sugar and cocoa exchange has decided to update its certified stock data daily instead of weekly. As of January 13 reported stocks fell by 250 bags to 23,138 bags. The decline was in Miami where stocks fell to 17,269 bags from 17,519 bags previously. There were no bags pending grading or recertification.

MEXICO - Mexico exported 390,137 bags of coffee in December 1996 compared to 421,445 bags exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (October/September) up to 874,469 bags which compares to 819,474 bags the same period in 1995/96. Exports in 1995/96 hit a record of 4.6 million bags.

SPAIN - Spain imported 312,695 bags of coffee in September 1996, 21 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.698 million bags, 11 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 2.2 per cent to 3.225 million bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Uganda (721,400 vs 488,500 bags), Brazil (234,500 vs 456,300 bags) and Colombia (271,500 vs 238,400 bags).

The country exported 385,900 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 29 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 6.7 per cent to 401,000 bags.
